parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of $\mathrm{C_{4}H_{8}}$, using the smallest whole-number coefficients.

rubric_rows.criterion: Balanced equation with the smallest whole-number coefficients: C4H8 + 6O2 → 4CO2 + 4H2O

rubric_rows.criterion: Applies the 4:1 mole ratio from the balanced equation to obtain 0.713 mol of CO2
common_errors: omits the mole ratio

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume, in L, occupied by the $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$ at the stated temperature and pressure.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the volume (about 21.8 L) using kelvins and consistent units for R
common_errors: uses the Celsius temperature

payload.title: Lewis structure, geometry and boiling points

stimulus.description: Consider the molecule $\mathrm{XeF_{4}}$ and the two compounds $\mathrm{CH_{3}OH}$ (32 g/mol, normal boiling point 338 K) and $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{6}}$ (30.1 g/mol, normal boiling point 185 K).

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a Lewis electron-dot diagram of $\mathrm{XeF_{4}}$ that shows all of its valence electrons.
parts.model_answer: XeF4 has 36 valence electrons in total: the diagram shows 4 bonds from the central atom to the other atoms, 2 lone pairs on the central atom, and the remaining lone pairs on the outer atoms.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws a Lewis diagram that accounts for all 36 valence electrons, with 4 bonded atoms and 2 lone pairs on the central atom
common_errors: omits the lone pairs on the central atom

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Use your diagram to identify the molecular geometry of $\mathrm{XeF_{4}}$ and the approximate bond angle.
parts.model_answer: square planar; bond angle 90° (six electron domains (four bonding pairs and two lone pairs) are arranged octahedrally with the lone pairs on opposite sides, giving a square planar shape).

rubric_rows.criterion: States square planar geometry and a bond angle of 90°
common_errors: reports the electron-domain geometry instead of the molecular geometry

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Is the $\mathrm{XeF_{4}}$ molecule polar or nonpolar? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: Nonpolar: the bond dipoles cancel because the shape is symmetric.

rubric_rows.criterion: States nonpolar and links it to the symmetric arrangement, in which the bond dipoles cancel
common_errors: decides by the polarity of the bonds alone

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The data in the stimulus show that $\mathrm{CH_{3}OH}$ has a higher boiling point than $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{6}}$ even though it has a similar molar mass. Explain this difference in terms of intermolecular forces.
parts.model_answer: CH3OH molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another, which are stronger than the attractions between C2H6 molecules, so more energy is needed to separate the molecules of CH3OH.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies hydrogen bonding between CH3OH molecules as stronger than the attractions between C2H6 molecules, which raises the boiling point
common_errors: says covalent bonds within the molecules break when the liquid boils

payload.title: Equilibrium expression, Q versus K and disturbances

stimulus.description: At a certain temperature the equilibrium $\mathrm{A}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\,\mathrm{B}(g)$ has $K_c=0.5$ and is endothermic. A cylinder with a movable piston initially contains $[\mathrm{A}]=0.5\text{ M}$ and $[\mathrm{B}]=0.1\text{ M}$ at this temperature.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Write the equilibrium-constant expression, $K_c$, for the reaction.
parts.model_answer: $K_c=[\mathrm{B}]^2/[\mathrm{A}]$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes $[\mathrm{B}]^2/[\mathrm{A}]$ (products over reactant, with the coefficient as an exponent)
common_errors: omits the exponent 2

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the reaction quotient, $Q$, for the initial mixture and determine the direction in which the reaction proceeds.
parts.model_answer: $Q=0.1^2/0.5=0.02$, which is less than $K_c=0.5$, so the reaction proceeds toward the products.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates $Q\approx 0.02$ and states the direction as forward by comparing Q with K
common_errors: reverses the comparison of Q and K

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: After the system reaches equilibrium, the piston is moved so that the volume of the cylinder is doubled at constant temperature. Predict the direction of the shift and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The system shifts toward the products: the expansion lowers the concentrations, $Q$ becomes less than $K_c$, and the side with more moles of gas (two moles of B instead of one of A) is favored at lower pressure.

rubric_rows.criterion: States the shift toward the products and justifies it with Q becoming less than K (or the favored side having more moles of gas)
common_errors: says K changes with volume

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The temperature is then increased. Does the value of $K_c$ increase or decrease? Justify your answer using the sign of the enthalpy change.
parts.model_answer: $K_c$ increases: for an endothermic reaction heat acts as a reactant, so raising the temperature favors the products.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that $K_c$ increases because heat behaves as a reactant in an endothermic reaction
common_errors: says K does not depend on temperature
